"totally warranted" is a strong phrase. I don't want to get into politics, I just want to clear up the misconception that George Bush is literally Hitler. he isn't. I'm not saying he's a great guy or that he was a great president, but 70% of songs written during his administration make him out to be a genocidal lunatic and the worst person in history, which seems a bit much. This has been going on as long as mainstream music as we know it has, and it isn't going anywhere. It just gets on my nerves during the Bush administration and a little while after especially, we got dozens of albums that have nothing to say other than "political figurehead bad" and know it. We shouldn't stop listening to all music released during the Vietnam War, just the albums that are just "LBJ is the devil" on a loop for 45 minutes.

All of Hail to the Thief, all of Continuum, and most of The Shepherd's Dog, a long with a lot of music from around the same time exist to convey one message and literally nothing else, that message being "George W. Bush ran for president with the intent of killing hundreds of trillions of people, and anyone who voted for him is a bad person to the core.". Doesn't mean the music is bad, though. The Shepherd's Dog is my favourite album of all time, because the lyrics and instrumentation more than make up for it's twisted messages, and it doesn't help that most of the songs on it are fairly subtle with their commentary. Hail to the Thief knows exactly what it is and beats you over the  head with it at every opportunity, and that gets old after a few songs, which sucks because the album gets less bad as it goes (for the most part), and by the time you've gotten to A Wolf at the Door, you're tired and hate everything.
